17427173028668895626: Jarilo: God of Spring and War Analysis Folklore Expert: Chico One of the earliest historical references to the god is in the biography of a diplomat from the Saya kingdom, about 1,800 years before the Eternal Freeze. On his expedition, he came across a tribe who happened to be celebrating the god of war, Jarroway. Experts from before the Eternal Freeze believed Jarroway to be the precursor of Jarilo. Around 1,200 years ago, in the northern region of Nycatha, a festival known as "Jarilo" was celebrated in late spring or early summer. Groups of villagers would walk along the countryside, symbolizing the return of the god back into this world. His return meant fertility and vegetation. Experts from before the Eternal Freeze found traces of religious rituals in honor of this god. The death of a god was seen as a ritualistic sacrifice, and carries heavy symbolic meaning. Similar metaphors can be found in other mythologies: The bodies of dead gods creating the world, with blood turning into rivers, bones turning into mountains, hair turning into forests, and so on. With the emergence of the Eternal Freeze, the world of the gods gradually began to weaken. Until eventually, the house built from Jarilo's corpse could no longer support human life and collapsed, just like it did in the myth. It is clear the myth's ending was influenced by the Eternal Freeze and the new religions. Before the Eternal Freeze, Jarilo was the typical "birth-death-rebirth" god of nature, whose mythological cycle was the same as that of crops in the northern region of Nycatha, from sowing to growing to harvesting (viewed as crop destruction). However, after the Eternal Freeze, the seasonal cycle was broken, replaced by Belobog's unique climate. In the myth, this climate change is explained by the household affairs between the gods. It's worth mentioning that in the story, Jarilo goes on a journey from an unfaithful bum to a loyal husband. By the end of the story, he sought redemption from Perun, paying a heavy price for his indiscretions. The changes in Jarilo here were thought to be related to the changing lunar phases, a projection of human understanding on natural phenomena. This understanding continued to hold after the Eternal Freeze emerged and people could no longer observe the moon's phase changes. There was a lack of understanding of such astronomical phenomena, so people were more inclined to draw a moral conclusion to the story — this god's endless cycle of birth-death-rebirth was the price to pay for his love.

The Smiling Hero, the League of Bliss... Even just a glance at their many nicknames speaks volumes about the public's affection for them. According to statistics, over the past two years, the Daybreak Squadron has solved 14 theft or robbery cases, 22 small-scale mutations caused by calamities, and assisted the Department of Aberration Defense in solving numerous medium and small cases. Meanwhile, the 4 performers have been actively involved in community work, holding a charity performance once every 2 weeks on average, and their "Superhero Safety Training" activities in Seafeld City have been well-received. Just like Fulwish who brought them to the stage, Daybreak Squadron has become an idol in many people's hearts. Hero or Actor? While the Daybreak Squadron's popularity has been surging among both teenagers and the elderly, some people believe that what Daybreak Squadron does could be achieved through simpler methods by the IPC and Department of Aberration Defense. In their eyes, the actors' activities are just like locals playing make-believe, orchestrated by Fulwish TV for publicity. I've seen this kind of plot so many times in Interastral Peace Entertainment that it's getting boring. — Pearluxe Corp Employee When in Planarcadia, do as the Planarcadia folks do! I'm actually enjoying this. It's like an immersive hero stage play. — Tourist from Capital of Passion The Department of Aberration Defense suppressing calamities? Not nearly as fun as watching heroes duke it out in tight suits! — Student of Graphia Academy Daybreak Squadron came to visit me at the hospital and brought lots of delicious treats. They're real heroes! — Patient at Duomension City Secondary Hospital Who Will Protect the World? Indeed, Daybreak Squadron may not possess world-saving powers like those in traditional hero stories such as the Astral Express. But does this mean their actions are meaningless? In an era where our hearts are gradually running dry, the birth of heroes is necessary. They symbolize the spirit of "what I choose to do," and now more than ever, as the Antimatter Legion's menace escalates, people desperately yearn for heroes they can call their own. Some say that after the Bloodstained Games, Planarcadia entered 15 years of peace and prosperity, a period free from major disasters, which they credit to the IPC's ramped-up investment in Planarcadia. However, I believe what truly protected us were the countless heroes who, like Daybreak Warriors, devoted everything to this land. — Shopkeeper from Seafeld City What Planarcadia needs is not an Emanator, but a "person" who truly respects us and walks beside us as equals. — Director of Fulwish TV Does Planarcadia need superheroes? I think it does. Even the Interastral Peace Corporation needs the Amber Lord to set a standard in people's hearts. Daybreak Squadron isn't irreplaceable. But they are ours, and that is what matters.
